body:
Hi @konard, thank you for the report. Generally I'm not too thrilled about the verbose sloppy issue description. Nevertheless I could reproduce the issue and the provided fix might make sense. Here's a quick version of my observations, to spare any other reviewers from this verbose slop. Having a server which sends early RST and then using `https://` to connect to this server, prevents lychee from retrying. Interestingly enough with `http://` the behaviour differs. Applying the following diff makes lychee retry the connections in the HTTPS case as well. I didn't yet fully grasp what is going on, but it shouldn't hurt to examine the inner errors more closely. ```patch diff --git a/lychee-lib/src/retry.rs b/lychee-lib/src/retry.rs index 0021c73a..ca059379 100644 --- a/lychee-lib/src/retry.rs +++ b/lychee-lib/src/retry.rs @@ -30,8 +30,8 @@ impl RetryExt for reqwest::Error { fn should_retry(&self) -> bool { if self.is_timeout() { true - } else if self.is_connect() { - false + } else if dbg!(self).is_connect() { + get_source_error_type::(self).is_some_and(should_retry_io) } else if self.is_body() || self.is_decode() || self.is_builder() || self.is_redirect() { false } else if self.is_request() { @@ -121,6 +121,13 @@ impl RetryExt for Status { /// Classifies an `io::Error` into retryable or not. fn should_retry_io(error: &io::Error) -> bool { + if let Some(inner) = error + .get_ref() + .and_then(|inner| inner.downcast_ref::()) + { + return should_retry_io(inner); + } + matches!( error.kind(), io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset | io::ErrorKind::ConnectionAborted | io::ErrorKind::TimedOut ``` Another good question is if and how we should/could test this with a new testcase. (reuse the python script?) @katrinafyi @mre Any thoughts on this?
How to reproduce

Command: `python3 server.py` with below script and then running `echo 'https://127.0.0.1:8443' | cargo run - --host-stats` ```python import socket import struct import time port = 8443 server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) server.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1) server.bind(("127.0.0.1", port)) server.listen(16) print(f"listening on 127.0.0.1:{port}", flush=True) started = time.monotonic() attempts = 0 while True: connection, _ = server.accept() attempts += 1 print(f"attempt {attempts} at +{time.monotonic() - started:.2f}s", flush=True) connection.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0)) connection.close() ```

Current downstream confirmation: the latest release endpoint still returns lychee 0.24.2 (2026-11-14). We retain a bounded external retry adapter in https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 for this reported connect-reset gap.

The minimal HTTPS RST server in this issue remains the relevant reproduction. Our offline regression tests preserve failure for permanent 404 responses, bound retries for unanswered connections and transient 429/5xx statuses, and reuse the same accepted statuses and user agent. Increasing lychee's retry count alone cannot change the connect-phase classifier.

The existing proposed fix that examines connect-phase I/O errors and unwraps nested `io::Error` values would let us remove the adapter once released. This records the consumer workaround rather than duplicate the report.
